status.label: Recheck the scaled-display pointer indicator on current stable
status.detail: With non-100% Windows display scaling, remapping CapsLock to Ctrl reportedly offsets Windows' built-in Ctrl pointer-location indicator; the reporter reproduced it on a 2024 build but not on current PowerToys.

judgment.rationale: The report contains detailed steps: on a fresh Windows session with non-100% scaling, remap CapsLock to Ctrl and compare Windows' built-in Ctrl pointer indicator with PowerToys' indicator; the Windows indicator is displaced toward the lower-right and the issue disappears at 100% scaling. The reporter reproduced this on a newly installed 2024-era PowerToys build, but there is no current supported-build confirmation. Related #11878 concerns whether the Windows indicator works after swapping Ctrl and Alt and is not the same offset/scaling symptom. Ask for the current-build result and exact display scaling before deciding whether a DPI-related PowerToys investigation remains warranted.
evidence: The original report lists PowerToys 0.73.0, elevated operation, and a fresh Windows session with non-100% display scaling.
CapsLock-to-Ctrl reportedly offsets Windows' built-in Ctrl pointer-location indicator toward the lower-right; PowerToys' own pointer indicator remains correctly placed.
Changing Windows display scaling to 100% reportedly removes the discrepancy.
The reporter reproduced the symptom again on a newly installed PowerToys build in 2024, but has not confirmed it on v0.102.3001.
Open #11878 discusses the Ctrl/Alt remap interaction with the same Windows pointer-location feature, but its reported behavior is different and does not establish a duplicate.
judgment.recommended_action: Ask whether the offset still reproduces on v0.102.3001 and record the exact scaling percentage and display layout.

fix_assessment.rationale: The DPI-dependent symptom was reproduced on a 2024 build, but current-build behavior is unknown; #11878 describes a different Ctrl/Alt indicator limitation and does not cover this offset defect.

issue_context.summary: On non-100% Windows display scaling, remapping CapsLock to Ctrl reportedly shifts Windows' built-in pointer-location indicator while PowerToys' indicator remains aligned.
known_information: The report lists PowerToys 0.73.0 and tests from a fresh Windows session with non-100% scaling.
The mapping is CapsLock to Ctrl; the Windows Ctrl pointer-location indicator is displaced toward the lower-right while the PowerToys indicator is correctly placed.
The reporter says changing display scaling to 100% removes the discrepancy and reproduced it again on a newly installed build in 2024.
No current supported-build retest is present.
inferences: The dependency on non-100% scaling suggests a DPI-sensitive interaction, but the report does not establish the responsible code path.
Issue #11878 shares the Windows indicator but describes a different Ctrl/Alt remapping behavior, not the same display-coordinate offset.
issue_context.analysis: The report has a specific trigger, comparison and workaround, so preserve those details. Current v0.102.3001 behavior and the exact scale/display layout are the only missing evidence needed before investigating a potentially DPI-related remap interaction.
initial_investigation: Read the issue body, all three comments, labels, and attached screenshots; the screenshots show Windows' misplaced indicator beside PowerToys' correctly placed indicator.
Compared the linked #11878 report; it covers the same Windows feature but a different Ctrl/Alt behavior and is not a duplicate.

information_gaps.information: Whether the Windows indicator offset still occurs with CapsLock-to-Ctrl on v0.102.3001, and the exact Windows scaling percentage and display layout used
information_gaps.why_needed: The issue was last confirmed on a 2024 build; a current result determines whether a PowerToys defect remains, while scale/layout details make the report reproducible.
information_gaps.how_to_collect: On v0.102.3001, repeat the CapsLock-to-Ctrl test with Windows' Show location of pointer when I press the CTRL key enabled; report the display scale percentage(s), monitor layout, and whether switching to 100% still removes the offset.

comment.body: Thanks for the detailed CapsLock-to-Ctrl test and for confirming that the Windows indicator was displaced on a newly installed build in 2024 while PowerToys' indicator stayed aligned. Could you confirm whether the same offset still occurs on v0.102.3001, and include the exact display-scaling percentage(s) and monitor layout? Please also say whether changing the scaling to 100% still removes it.
